_about: Gold key points for the Phase 3 eval (docs/llm-eval.md). Written 2026-09-26 from each case's findings, BEFORE any LLM ran on these cases (the spike saw 09, 10, 17, 18 - all in the dev split). rootCause = what M3 requires; mustName = identifiers M3 requires; mustNotClaim = case-specific traps M4 checks on top of the common list in docs/llm-eval.md.

01-demo-order_items-order_id.rootCause: The join to order_items on order_items.order_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~500,000 order_items rows; with the index it looks up only the items of the matching orders.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the orders.customer_id scan (a different finding)

02-demo-orders-customer_id.rootCause: Postgres reads all ~200,000 orders and keeps only the few (est. 8) for one customer; the index lets it jump to that customer's rows.
mustNotClaim: that the index removes the ORDER BY sort (no R4 finding here)

03-demo-orders-created_at.rootCause: The query sorts orders by created_at only to return the first few rows (ORDER BY ... LIMIT); an index in created_at order lets Postgres read rows already in order and stop early.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the customers.country scan or the orders.customer_id join (other findings)

04-demo-events-customer_id-occurred_at.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~300,000 events to find a few (est. 7) for one customer, then sorts them by occurred_at for the LIMIT; the two-column index finds that customer's events already in occurred_at order.

05-demo-orders-status-created_at.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~200,000 orders to keep one status (est. ~23,500 rows) and sorts them by created_at to return the first few; the index gives that status's rows already in created_at order, so it reads only the first few.
mustNotClaim: that the status filter alone is highly selective (est. ~12 % of rows)

06-demo-events-event_type.rootCause: To count one event type Postgres scans all ~300,000 events (est. ~20,800 match); the index lets it read only the matching entries.

07-demo-order_items-product_id.rootCause: The join from products to order_items on order_items.product_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~500,000 order_items rows; with the index it fetches only the items of the matching products.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the products.category scan (a different finding)

08-demo-events-payload.rootCause: The payload @> (containment) filter makes Postgres scan all ~300,000 events; a GIN index can answer containment lookups directly. PgLens could not check this with the planner (HypoPG can't simulate GIN).
mustNotClaim: any cost drop, percentage or speed-up for this index
that the planner/HypoPG checked or validated it

09-tpch-lineitem-l_shipdate.rootCause: Inside this query, Postgres scans all ~600,000 lineitem rows to keep the few matching the l_shipdate filter (est. 1); the index lets it read only the matching date range.

10-tpch-lineitem-l_partkey.rootCause: The join from part to lineitem on lineitem.l_partkey has no index, so Postgres scans all ~600,000 lineitem rows; with the index it looks up only the lines of the matching parts.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the part.p_brand / p_container scans (other findings)

11-tpch-lineitem-l_suppkey.rootCause: The join from supplier to lineitem on lineitem.l_suppkey has no index, so Postgres scans all ~600,000 lineitem rows; with the index it looks up only the matching suppliers' lines.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the supplier.s_nationkey join or the s_name sort (other findings)

12-tpch-lineitem-l_quantity.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~600,000 lineitem rows to keep the few (est. 268) that pass the filter; an index on l_quantity lets it read only the rows in the quantity range.
mustNotClaim: that the index covers l_shipmode or l_shipinstruct (same scan, not indexed by this rec)

13-tpch-lineitem-l_discount.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~600,000 lineitem rows to keep the few (est. 2) that pass the date, discount and quantity filters; an index on l_discount lets it read only rows in the discount range.
mustNotClaim: that the index covers l_shipdate or l_quantity

14-tpch-orders-o_custkey.rootCause: The join to orders on orders.o_custkey has no index, so Postgres scans all ~150,000 orders; with the index it looks up only the chosen customers' orders.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the customer.c_acctbal scan

15-tpch-partsupp-ps_suppkey.rootCause: The join from supplier to partsupp on partsupp.ps_suppkey has no index, so Postgres scans all ~80,000 partsupp rows; with the index it looks up only the matching suppliers' rows.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the supplier.s_nationkey join

16-tpch-orders-o_orderdate.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~150,000 orders to keep those in the o_orderdate range (est. 441); the index lets it read only that date range.
mustNotClaim: that the index fixes the o_custkey, c_nationkey or n_regionkey joins

17-job-movie_info-movie_id.rootCause: The join to movie_info on movie_info.movie_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~14.8 million movie_info rows; with the index it looks up only the rows of the movies it needs.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes any of the query's other 8 findings (other tables/columns)
that the query will then be fast overall

18-job-movie_info-info.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~14.8 million movie_info rows to keep the few (est. ~3,000) whose info matches; an index on info lets it read only those.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the movie_info.movie_id join or other findings

19-job-cast_info-movie_id.rootCause: The join to cast_info on cast_info.movie_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~36.2 million cast_info rows; with the index it looks up only the rows of the movies it needs.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the cast_info.person_id join or the cast_info.note scan (other findings)

20-job-cast_info-person_id.rootCause: The join to cast_info on cast_info.person_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~36.2 million cast_info rows; with the index it looks up only the rows of the people it needs.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the cast_info.movie_id join or the cast_info.note scan

21-job-cast_info-note.rootCause: Postgres scans all ~36.2 million cast_info rows to keep the few (est. ~6,400) whose note matches; an index on note lets it read only those.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the cast_info joins

22-job-cast_info-role_id.rootCause: The join to cast_info on cast_info.role_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~36.2 million cast_info rows; with the index it looks up only the rows with the role it needs.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the cast_info.movie_id or aka_name.person_id joins

23-job-movie_keyword-keyword_id.rootCause: The join to movie_keyword on movie_keyword.keyword_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~4.5 million movie_keyword rows; with the index it looks up only the rows of the few matching keywords.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the keyword.keyword scan or the movie_companies joins

24-job-movie_companies-movie_id.rootCause: The join to movie_companies on movie_companies.movie_id has no index, so Postgres scans all ~2.6 million movie_companies rows; with the index it looks up only the rows of the movies it needs.
mustNotClaim: that this index fixes the company_type_id join or the movie_keyword join
